summary: Production-hardening pass on /developers focused on the NEW Trust & Security section, the Security nav item, the KMS migration resource card, clean-session lifecycle (no login/cookies), and full responsiveness (desktop 1920x1080, tablet 768x1024, mobile 390x844). 23/23 desktop checks pass. Full lifecycle (sandbox key -> proof -> verify with 'Proof is authentic & untampered' + 3 PASS checks) succeeds on both desktop and mobile with a fresh, unauthenticated session. All 14 primary resource/doc/SDK/footer links return HTTP 200. ONE responsive bug found: the top nav horizontally overflows at 768px (tablet) viewport (scrollWidth=934 > viewport=768), caused by 7 nav items + 'Demo' + 'Admin' + 'API Docs' cluster.

Top nav contains 7 section links + Demo + Admin + API Docs button; right cluster extends to right=934, causing the whole page to be horizontally scrollable on tablets in portrait. Screenshot shows 'Demo / Admin / A...' clipped at the right edge. The hidden-sm-inline class for Admin only collapses BELOW 640px; at 768px Admin (right=819) and API Docs (right=934) are both rendered alongside all 7 section links, exceeding viewport.

issues: Right-side action buttons (Demo / Admin / API Docs) push the page width to 934px, producing horizontal scroll. Consider collapsing into a menu below `lg` breakpoint, or hiding Admin/Demo on tablet, or wrapping into a second row.

action_items: FIX (MEDIUM): Resolve tablet (768px) horizontal overflow caused by DevNav right cluster. Suggested options: (a) hide Admin link at <lg breakpoint (it's already 'hidden sm:inline-flex' - bump to 'hidden lg:inline-flex'); (b) collapse the section nav into a hamburger menu below `lg`; (c) hide 'Demo' link below `lg`. Currently scrollWidth=934 vs viewport=768.
OPTIONAL (LOW): Add data-testid='sandbox-key-card' / 'first-proof-card' / 'verify-proof-card' to the three Playground wrapper containers so responsive stacking can be asserted via testid.
critical_code_review_comments: DevNav: 'Admin' has 'hidden sm:inline-flex' (visible from 640px+), and the 7 section nav links remain inline at 768px alongside Demo/Admin/API Docs button; combined width exceeds the 768px tablet viewport. The breakpoint strategy should escalate hides to 'lg' (1024px) or introduce a menu collapse below `lg`.
TrustArchitecture fetches /api/developer on every mount with no caching; if the user toggles between pages frequently it will refetch. Low-impact since payload is tiny.
TrustArchitecture footer string uses backticks: signing.supported_providers.join(', ') with no fallback when array missing — minor robustness gap.

success_rate.frontend: 96% (24/25 hard checks pass; 1 tablet responsiveness bug)

test_credentials: Not required — verified the entire flow works with NO login, NO cookies, NO prior auth (clean session).
seed_data_creation: None — used live backend; generated sandbox keys pfp_sandbox_f14c3620... (desktop) and pfp_sandbox_7f675c94... (mobile).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Trust section fetch URL: GET /api/developer (returns .signing.{current_capability, architecture_readiness, planned_enhancements, algorithm, active_provider, active_mode, supported_providers}). Verified live values: active_provider='local' (seed-env), supported_providers=['aws','azure','gcp','local'], algorithm='Ed25519'. Verify outcome string MUST be exactly 'Proof is authentic & untampered'. Tablet 768px nav overflow is the only outstanding bug.
rca of the issue: Tablet horizontal overflow RCA: At viewport=768, DevNav renders the entire 7-item section nav + 'Demo' (testid dev-nav-demo) + 'Admin' (testid dev-nav-admin, hidden only below 640px via 'hidden sm:inline-flex') + 'API Docs' (testid dev-nav-api-docs, always visible). The right action cluster (.flex.items-center.gap-2.shrink-0) stretches from x=685 to x=934, overflowing the 768px viewport by 166px. Reproduction: open https://pfp-pilot-ready.preview.emergentagent.com/developers at 768x1024 -> body has horizontal scroll. Mitigation: change 'hidden sm:inline-flex' on dev-nav-admin (and optionally dev-nav-demo) to 'hidden lg:inline-flex', OR add a tablet/mobile hamburger menu for the section nav.
